title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X smooth over S, n ≥ 0. The page defines an 'n-connexion projective' on X/S. This is an algebraic, characteristic-free, truncated version of a Cartan projective connection (projective structure).

Data (a). A Brauer–Severi (projective) bundle P over X with a section σ. Equivalently, after normalising the line quotient to O_X, an extension 0 → Ω → E → O_X → 0 of locally free O_X-modules with P = P(E). Equivalently, a pair (Ω, τ) with Ω locally free and τ an Ω-torsor; the class of τ is the extension class in H^1(X, Ω). Here Ω is the conormal bundle of σ(X) in P.

Data (b). An X-isomorphism between the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X ×_S X and the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of σ(X) in P. Equivalently, an isomorphism of augmented O_X-algebras
  P^n_{X/S} ≅ O_{P̂}/Ĵ^{n+1}.
Here P̂ is the formal completion along σ and Ĵ the ideal of the section. The right side is the τ-twist of the truncated algebra Sym^•(Ω)/Sym^{≥n+1}(Ω).

The twist makes sense by the previous page. The vector group Ω acts on Ŝ = O_{P̂} as the stabiliser of the marked point (the affine-translation part of the parabolic). It acts trivially on gr^•_Ĵ = Sym^•Ω. On J^n/J^{n+2}, a acts by f + g ↦ f + n·a·f + g. So it changes the extension class of Sym^nΩ by Sym^{n+1}Ω via the map v_n : Ω → Hom(Sym^nΩ, Sym^{n+1}Ω), v_n(a)(f) = af, with a factor −n (sign convention).

Low orders:
- n = 0: (b) is empty.
- n = 1: (b) amounts to an isomorphism (*) Ω ≅ Ω^1_{X/S}. In particular rk Ω equals the relative dimension r of X/S.
- n = 2: P^2_{X/S} is determined by its extension structure, an extension of Ω^1 by Sym^2Ω^1. This is a torsor under Hom(Ω^1, Sym^2Ω^1), essentially the class of the second-order jets. Condition (b) then says this canonical torsor must be identified with the push-out of τ along −v_1 : Ω → Hom(Ω, Sym^2Ω), transported via (*).

Consequence (completed on the next page). Contraction gives a retraction Hom(Ω, Sym^2Ω) → Ω whose composite with v_1 is (r+1)·id. So if r+1 is invertible on S, τ (hence E and P) is canonically determined by X/S. This is the classical fact that the 'Euler sequence' bundle of a projective structure is forced, up to the dual/sign convention, to be J^1(K^{-1/(r+1)}); its class is a multiple of c_1(K_X)/(r+1), i.e. the Atiyah class of K.

Purpose: set up a jet-theoretic, base-free notion of projective connection. The next page adds ∞-connections, flatness via stratifications (Grothendieck's crystalline viewpoint), and the question whether τ is canonical without hypotheses on dimension or characteristic. This serves the uniformisation theme of the cote.
errors: Minor: 'fibré de B.S. avec une section ⇔ extension 0→Ω→E→O_X→0' holds only after normalising the twist ambiguity of E so that the line quotient is O_X. This is implicitly done.
The sign/normalisation (−v_1 versus v_1, f/(1+a)^n) is convention-dependent; consistent with the previous page.

ideas.what: Definition of a (truncated) n-th order projective connection as an isomorphism between the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal of X×_S X and the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of a section of a P^r-bundle
ideas.modern_name: Cartan projective connection / projective structure formulated as a Cartan geometry via jets (osculating projective bundle); truncated 'order n' Cartan connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: É. Cartan (1924) for projective connections; Gunning, Kobayashi–Nagano (1960s–70s) for holomorphic versions; algebraic/positive-characteristic versions by Mochizuki (indigenous bundles, 1990s) and later Wakabayashi
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as I know; the jet formalism P^n_{X/S} is EGA IV 16. Unsure whether these notes circulated.

ideas.what: Ω-torsor description of a projective bundle with section (extension of O_X by Ω)
ideas.modern_name: Euler-type extension / parabolic reduction of a PGL_{r+1}-bundle

ideas.what: Second-order compatibility: the extension class of the 2-jets (Ω^1 by Sym^2Ω^1) must equal the push-out of τ along −v_1; contraction shows τ is determined by X when r+1 is invertible
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to projective structures via the class of P^2_{X/S} / Atiyah class of K_X divided by (r+1); E ≅ J^1(K^{-1/(r+1)})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (On uniformization of complex manifolds, 1978), Kobayashi–Ochiai, Molzon–Mortensen

missed.claim: A characteristic-free, base-relative hierarchy of 'n-projective connections' (n = 0, 1, 2, …, ∞) defined via infinitesimal neighbourhoods. The canonicity of the underlying torsor τ is derived from the n = 2 level when r+1 is invertible, and posed as an open question in general (next page). A careful treatment of truncated projective structures over arbitrary bases, especially when p | r+1, is not standard in the literature.
missed.quote: Une n-connexion projective sur X (rel. à S) est la donnée a) d'un fibré de B.S. P sur X avec une section ... b) Une X-isom. des voisinages inf. d'ordre n de la diagonale de X×_S X avec le voisinage inf. d'ordre n de la section dans P
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to projective structures and opers in positive and mixed characteristic (Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory, Wakabayashi's dormant opers and higher-dimensional Frobenius-projective structures), where the r+1 invertibility issue appears explicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early, scheme-theoretic jet definition of projective connections with truncation levels, plus the (r+1)-invertibility mechanism. The underlying mathematics is classical in differential geometry and later reappears in the opers/indigenous-bundle literature, but this exact algebraic formulation by Grothendieck is not, to my knowledge, documented.
transcription_corrections: 'τ un ...-torseur' should read 'τ un Ω-torseur' (or 'torseur sous Ω').
The map labelled '-u_1' is presumably '−v_1', matching the v_n of the previous page.
In b), '... ou ce qui revient au même[?] O_X-' continues as 'une iso. de O_X-Algèbres augmentées'.
